quality_guards: Flood alerts, flood warnings and severe flood warnings have different meanings, lead times and required actions.
Environment Agency warning registration does not cover surface-water or flash flooding.
Long-term flood risk describes land or area risk and not the exact likelihood that an individual building will flood.
Met Office warning colours combine impact and likelihood; yellow does not always mean low impact.
Weather warnings and Weather-Health Alerts are separate services with different purposes.
Current weather, health, road and rail operational states require live checking because they can change after publication.
National Highways closures can change at short notice and become less certain further ahead.
Level-crossing maps and models can lag closures and do not guarantee live crossing condition.
Work-related violence requires a work connection; unrelated personal disputes are kept outside that definition.
Manual-handling controls depend on task, load, worker and environment; no universal legal weight limit is inferred.
Chemical response guidance is substance-, route-, incident- and site-specific.
NHS 999 and 111 outcomes depend on clinical triage and do not guarantee a particular response resource.
Official-source context is not converted into exact parcel-level probability.
Live 130-candidate/16-endpoint parity, browser DOM/console acceptance and publisher readback remain required.
No second runner was started; the stale single-runner recovery blocker remains OPEN.
